name: Arrays and Strings
description: Contiguous memory structures and sequence algorithms for fast indexed access, slicing, windowing, and transformation.

name: Hash Tables
description: Associative key-value structures utilizing hashing functions to provide expected amortized O(1) lookup, insertion, and deletion.

name: Linked Lists
description: Dynamic sequential data structures where elements point to their successor and/or predecessor nodes, enabling O(1) insertion and deletion at known positions.

name: Stacks and Queues
description: Linear abstract data types governing First-In-First-Out (FIFO) or Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) access, monotonic properties, and deque operations.

name: Trees and Graphs
description: Hierarchical and network data structures representing nodes and edges, including Binary Search Trees, Heaps, Tries, and adjacency graphs.
characteristics: Shortest path and spanning tree models

name: Searching and Sorting
description: Algorithms designed to locate elements in ordered and unordered data collections, reorder sequences, and partition spaces efficiently.

name: Recursion and Backtracking
description: Algorithmic strategies solving problems by decomposing into sub-problems and systematically exploring state spaces with pruning.

name: Greedy Algorithms
description: Optimization paradigms making locally optimal choices at each stage with the expectation of finding a global optimum.

name: Dynamic Programming
description: Algorithmic technique solving complex problems by breaking them into overlapping subproblems and storing intermediate solutions (memoization or tabulation).

name: Bit Manipulation
description: Low-level bitwise operations operating directly on binary representations of integers for ultra-fast, zero-overhead computation.

name: Advanced Data Structures
description: Specialized data structures combining multiple primitives to solve domain-specific problems, such as Disjoint-Set Union, Bloom Filters, and Consistent Hash Rings.
